title: Factors Associated With the Autonomy of Patients Treated by Haemodialysis in Community Centres. A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: All patients receiving haemodialysis in community centres in a French region on December 31, 2021. MEASUREMENTS: Patient characteristics and multiple dimensions of patient autonomy were recorded. Multivariate analyses assessed associations between patient factors and technical autonomy. RESULTS: Among 507 patients, 304 were treated in self-care units and 203 in satellite haemodialysis units. Patients in satellite haemodialysis units had a median age of 69 years (IQR 59-78; range 24-90), compared with 66 years (IQR 54-75; range 22-91) in self-care haemodialysis units. They also had more comorbidities. Younger age was associated with greater autonomy in arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), setting the haemodialysis machine (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), and programming it (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Autonomy differed significantly between centres, with centre affiliation significantly associated (p < .001) with autonomy for the arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing and machine-related tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Patient characteristics in self-care haemodialysis units did not fully explain autonomy for haemodialysis tasks. Considerable variability between centres was observed, suggesting that centre-related factors may contribute to differences in patient autonomy.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units.

title: Maintaining IV Patency Throughout Pharmacokinetic Studies Through a Needle-Free Blood Draw Device.
abstract: 8 8 9 Pharmacokinetic (PK) studies require temporally precise measurements of drug concentrations in biological matrices, most commonly whole blood or plasma. However, repeated venous sampling may increase participant burden and complicate PK-intensive study designs. Needle-free blood collection devices that access peripheral intravenous (IV) catheters may provide an alternative approach to repeated venipuncture while maintaining sampling schedules and specimen quality. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of integrating the PIVO Pro needle-free blood collection device into a PK-intensive human laboratory study of inhaled Δ-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ-THC), Δ-THC, and placebo. Participants completed a screening visit and three dosing visits conducted in a university research facility equipped with a full-scale driving simulator. During each dosing visit, venous blood samples were collected at nine time points over approximately 8 h through an indwelling peripheral IV catheter using the PIVO device. All participants reported that study procedures, including blood collection, were acceptable. Approximately 40% of vascular access sites required replacement, most commonly within the first hour and typically associated with poor initial blood return. Despite slower flow compared with standard venipuncture, sampling was generally sufficient to maintain the PK sampling schedule. One mild adverse event related to vascular access (localized bruising) was observed. These findings demonstrate the operational feasibility of needle-free blood collection through indwelling IV catheters in a PK-intensive research protocol conducted outside a traditional clinical research unit. Further studies are warranted to compare analytical performance and access durability relative to conventional venous sampling approaches.

title: SEVERE RETINAL NONPERFUSION IS ASSOCIATED WITH FEWER RETINAL LESIONS ON ULTRAWIDE-FIELD FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPHY IN PROLIFERATIVE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY.
abstract: PURPOSE: To explore the relationship between the number of retinal lesions observed on ultrawide-field fundus photography (UWF-FP) and the nonperfusion index (NPI) quantified on UWF fluorescein angiography in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR). METHODS: The NPI was measured on early-phase UWF fluorescein angiography in 100 eyes from 100 patients with PDR, including both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Eyes were divided into quartiles based on NPI values. Red dots (microaneurysms, retinal hemorrhages, and intraretinal microvascular abnormalities), venous beading, cotton-wool spots, and white thread-like arterioles were counted on UWF-FP. RESULTS: The mean NPI values for quartiles one to four were 2.8 ± 1.1%, 8.5 ± 2.1%, 17.3 ± 4.5%, and 42.8 ± 12.2%, respectively. Eyes in the highest NPI quartile (quartile 4) had significantly fewer retinal lesions on UWF-FP (76.1 ± 50.6) and fewer cotton-wool spots compared with those in the lowest NPI quartile, which showed 253.0 ± 165.5 retinal lesions ( P < 0.001). White thread-like arterioles were present in 80.0% of eyes in quartile four and none in quartile 1. Patients in quartile four were predominantly type 2 diabetics with higher rates of end-stage kidney disease, peripheral neuropathy, lower-extremity peripheral artery disease, and prior limb amputation or revascularization. CONCLUSION: In patients with poorly controlled, long-standing type 2 diabetes complicated by renal failure, peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, or lower-limb amputation, fluorescein angiography should be considered when highly ischemic PDR is suspected, particularly in the presence of white thread-like arterioles, as it may otherwise appear milder on color fundus photography.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: To explore the relationship between the number of retinal lesions observed on ultrawide-field fundus photography (UWF-FP) and the nonperfusion index (NPI) quantified on UWF fluorescein angiography in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR). METHODS: The NPI was measured on early-phase UWF fluorescein angiography in 100 eyes from 100 patients with PDR, including both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Eyes were divided into quartiles based on NPI values.

title: Circulating Natural Killer Cells in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Peripheral Neuropathy Are Altered in Their Frequency and Exhibit Impaired Functions and Angiogenic Activities.
abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), a severe vascular complication associated with amputation and high mortality, exhibit chronic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. We previously reported an increased frequency of natural killer (NK) cells in advanced CLTI; however, whether NK cell alterations are already present in patients with peripheral neuropathy, which often precedes diabetic foot lesions with or without distal macroangiopathy, remains unclear. We conducted an observational pilot study to assess circulating NK cell frequency by flow cytometry and inflammatory plasma cytokines profiling by ELISA in 177 subjects stratified into five groups: healthy controls (HC, n = 25); T2DM without neurovascular complications (D, n = 26); non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM without foot lesions (N, n = 40); non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM with lower-limb ulcers/lesions/osteomyelitis (N1, n = 42); and macrovascular revascularized neuropathic T2DM with ulcers/lesions/osteomyelitis (NV, n = 44). NK cell subset frequencies were evaluated in an independent cohort of patients with non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM (n = 22) and healthy controls (n = 23). NKs were further characterized for degranulation capacity, secretome composition, and pro-angiogenic activity in vitro and in vivo (Hirudo verbana). NK cell frequency was significantly increased in patients with non-macrovascular neuropathic T2DM compared with controls and was accompanied by elevated plasma levels of soluble mediators associated with NK cell activation and function, including TNF-α, IL-12p70, MCP-1, and IL-4. NKs from these patients exhibited impaired degranulation and reduced angiogenic capacity in vitro and in vivo. Their secretome is characterized by decreased release of pro-angiogenic factors and increased secretion of mediators involved in monocyte/macrophage recruitment, resulting in enhanced macrophage recruitment in vivo. If confirmed in larger cohorts, higher frequency and functional impairment of circulating NKs may act as novel therapeutic targets and prognostic biomarkers in peripheral vascular complications of T2DM.

title: Performance of Western HA-VTE risk models in East Asian populations: a prospective multicenter study.
abstract: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up. The 90-day HA-VTE incidence was 2.54%. All 5 models showed moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.726-0.759). Caprini, Padua, and Intermountain models did not differ significantly (DeLong test, P> .05). Caprini had the highest sensitivity (0.83) but classified 42.6% of patients as being at high risk. Padua and Intermountain favored specificity (0.75-0.81) with lower sensitivity (0.64-0.67). Clinical model selection should align with specific balances between sensitivity and utility. In surgical inpatients, Caprini performed best (AUC, 0.804; sensitivity, 0.90; negative predictive value, 1.00), although its more than 40 input variables limit practical use. Calibration was generally acceptable. Performance varied across subgroups. The prophylaxis subgroup showed attenuated performance, with reduced discrimination (eg, Caprini AUC decreased to 0.682) and less stable calibration. Western HA-VTE models have moderate predictive value in East Asian inpatient populations. Performance differs across subgroups. Local recalibration and development of simpler, population-specific scores are needed.

We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up.

title: The retrieved venous thrombus as a translational platform: a methodologic roadmap for venous immunothrombosis.
abstract: Percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy is now widely used for iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) across several device platforms, and every procedure yields intact human thrombus that is routinely discarded. Whether this material can be developed into a translational resource linking thrombus biology to clinical outcome has not been systematically addressed. A narrative, non-systematic review was performed. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched (January 2010 to August 2026) for studies addressing the biology, histopathology and translational analysis of mechanically retrieved venous thrombi, supplemented by reference-list, trial-registry and congress hand-searching. Published venous series remain small and largely confined to descriptive histology, disconnected from longitudinal outcomes. Intra-thrombus biology could address venous-specific questions that peripheral biomarkers and imaging alone cannot: post-thrombotic syndrome, incomplete recanalization, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and cancer-associated thrombosis. A device-agnostic framework is proposed, comprising structured intra-procedural sampling at the level of the case rather than the anatomical region, centralized specimen processing under harmonized quality standards, a tiered analytic pipeline anchored on quantitative immunohistochemistry, paired peripheral-biomarker collection, pre-specified hypotheses with feasibility-based sample sizes, and biobank infrastructure embedded in existing trial platforms. The equivalent programme in arterial thrombectomy supplies transferable methodology, subject to explicit boundary conditions. The retrieved venous thrombus is among the more underused translational specimens in vascular medicine. A standardized, registry-embedded characterization framework could accelerate progress toward precision venous thrombosis medicine.

Whether this material can be developed into a translational resource linking thrombus biology to clinical outcome has not been systematically addressed. A narrative, non-systematic review was performed.

title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018). CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes.

title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression. RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023.

title: Short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children represents a significant and growing global health burden. This study aims to report the short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted to assess outcomes in pediatric patients with various types of hemodialysis access. This prospective cohort study included all consecutive pediatric patients with ESRD who presented to the Vascular and Endovascular Surgery Department at a tertiary hospital from October 2022 to October 2023. RESULTS: The study included 50 pediatric patients, with a mean age of 10.5 ± 5.7 years. The cohort was predominantly female 35 (70%), while males accounted for 15 (30%) The overall technical success rate remained high at 45 (90%). The failure rate was 5 (10%). CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that pediatric arteriovenous fistulas (predominantly autogenous), when carefully planned and executed, can achieve high primary success and patency rates, with manageable complications in children with end-stage renal disease.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children represents a significant and growing global health burden. This study aims to report the short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted to assess outcomes in pediatric patients with various types of hemodialysis access.

title: Inferior Vena Cava Filters in Adolescents with Thromboembolic Disease: Technical Outcomes, Retrieval, and the Role of Skeletal Maturity.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate technical success, periprocedural safety and retrieval outcomes of inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) placement in adolescents with venous thromboembolism and to determine whether retrieval failure is associated with skeletal maturity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-center retrospective review of 26 IVCF placed in 25 patients with iliocaval or iliofemoral thrombosis (mean age 15.8 ± 2.2 years; range 9-18) between 2006 and 2024. Skeletal maturity was graded by Risser stage. Retrieval was attempted once the initial indication had resolved and anticoagulation was feasible. RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in every case; mean caval diameter was 17.9 ± 3.0 mm. Retrieval was attempted in 22 of 26 filters and succeeded in 19 (86% of attempts, 79% by intent to retrieve, 73% overall). One successful retrieval required a second attempt with an adjunctive loop-snare maneuver. Median indwelling time was 89 days (range 1-489). All three unsuccessful retrievals occurred at Risser stage 3 or below (3 of 7 versus 0 of 15 attempted; P = .02), not explained by caval diameter (P = .33). Seven filters (27%) remained in situ. No periprocedural adverse events occurred. Both retained filters assessed by CT showed caval wall penetration, one with strut fracture and asymptomatic migration at 16 years; chronic caval occlusion developed in one patient. CONCLUSION: Off-label IVCF placement in adolescents achieved high technical and retrieval success. Retrieval failure was confined to skeletally immature patients and was not explained by caval diameter. Strut fracture with migration at long-term imaging reinforces the need for timely retrieval.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: To evaluate technical success, periprocedural safety and retrieval outcomes of inferior vena cava filter (IVCF) placement in adolescents with venous thromboembolism and to determine whether retrieval failure is associated with skeletal maturity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-center retrospective review of 26 IVCF placed in 25 patients with iliocaval or iliofemoral thrombosis (mean age 15.8 ± 2.2 years; range 9-18) between 2006 and 2024. Skeletal maturity was graded by Risser stage.

title: Post-embolization dynamic changes in Obsidio Conformable Embolic: volume and radiodensity analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the temporal dynamic and clinical remodeling of the Obsidio™ Conformable Embolic (Obsidio) post endovascular delivery using longitudinal quantitative CT volumetry and Hounsfield unit (HU) attenuation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 21 patients (30 vessels) embolized with Obsidio for acute hemorrhage or hypervascular tumor between 2023 and 2026. Patients had at least two follow-up computed tomography (CT) scans. The primary endpoint was the percent change in embolic cast volume and HU attenuation, measured using standardized Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) segmentation tools. Secondary endpoints included assessment for recanalization. RESULTS: All embolizations were technically successful (100%). On the first follow-up CT (median 12 days), the mean Obsidio volume was 89.33 ± 13.86% of the original volume (p = 0.0002). On the second follow-up (median 36 days), the volume was 79.51 ± 19.76% of baseline volume (p = 0.0004), representing 20.49% reduction. On third follow-up CT (median 76 days), volume was 85.2 ± 18.92% (p = 0.047). On the fourth follow-up CT, volume was 66.76 ± 16.9% (p = 0.0048). On the fifth follow-up CT, volume was 60.15 ± 3.15% (p = 0.00001) The average volume reduction rate decelerated from 0.99%/day to 0.71%/day to 0.17%/day then stabilized at 0.2%/day. Concurrently, mean Hounsfield unit attenuation increased by 4.85% (p = 0.06) on the second follow-up CT scan. No evidence of recanalization, distal embolization, or cast fragmentation was observed on any of CT scans. CONCLUSION: The Obsidio embolic cast undergoes progressive reduction in volume and increase in HU attenuation over time without evidence of vessel recanalization. This temporal dynamic of Obsidio embolic is consistent with bioresorption of its gelatin and water components, supporting the concept of persistent occlusion via in vivo remodeling.

title: Early versus late venous thromboembolism in patients with newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurs in 20-30% and 9.2% of patients with glioblastoma and grade 3 IDH mutant (IDHmut) gliomas respectively, with highest risk during the first months post-surgery. We sought to identify risk factors for early versus late VTE in high-grade gliomas and evaluated the recently proposed 'GliomaPredictVTE' tool. METHODS: We included 894 patients with newly-diagnosed glioblastoma and grade 3-4 IDHmut gliomas from 2010-2023. Competing-risk analysis estimated VTE cumulative incidence (CumInc), segmented linear regression model identified the change-point between early versus late VTE, and competing-risk regression model identified significant risk factors. GliomaPredictVTE-predicted 6- and 12-month VTE risks were compared to observed CumInc. RESULTS: The estimated 6- and 12-month VTE CumInc was 21.5% and 26.4%, respectively for IDHwt glioblastoma versus 6.3% and 8.3%, respectively for IDHmut gliomas. The VTE CumInc increased rapidly during the first 6 months post-surgery, followed by a more gradual rise thereafter, with a change-point around 6 months. On multivariable analyses, 'Early VTE' (within 6 months post-surgery) was significantly associated with older age, limb weakness, ambulation dependence, and radiotherapy alone; 'Late VTE' (6 months to 5 years) with older age and smoking. GliomaPredictVTE substantially underestimated VTE incidence in our population, with a mean predicted 6- and 12-month risks of 11.0% and 17.4%, versus observed CumInc of 19.9% (p < 0.001) and 23% (p = 0.008), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Distinct risk profiles between early and late VTE support prospective studies of primary prophylaxis in high-risk patients, particularly in the first 6 months post-surgery. GliomaPredictVTE significantly underestimates VTE incidence in this population.

title: A 78-Year-Old Man With a Previously Stable Atherosclerotic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Presenting With Impending Rupture Following COVID-19.
abstract: BACKGROUND Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture is a life-threatening condition. Although elective repair is generally guided by aneurysm size, impending rupture can occur when rapid aneurysmal expansion or periaortic inflammatory changes develop before overt hemodynamic deterioration. This report describes the case of a 78-year-old man with a previously stable 43-mm atherosclerotic AAA who presented with impending rupture after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). CASE REPORT A 78-year-old Japanese man with a known AAA under imaging surveillance developed fever and was diagnosed with COVID-19 by nasopharyngeal polymerase chain reaction testing. Seven days later, he was admitted for recurrent fever, cough, poor appetite, and elevated inflammatory markers. His medical history included hypertension, heavy smoking, advanced chronic kidney disease, and diffuse atherosclerotic disease. The aneurysm had shown minimal growth over 2 years, with a stable maximum short-axis diameter of approximately 43 mm on serial computed tomography. After admission, C-reactive protein levels initially decreased but rose again on hospital day 11, accompanied by new-onset mild low back pain and no marked blood pressure elevation or hemodynamic instability. Repeat non-contrast abdominal computed tomography performed 18 days after COVID-19 diagnosis demonstrated rapid AAA expansion from 43 mm to 51 mm within 2 months, with periaortic fat stranding, consistent with impending rupture. Urgent endovascular aneurysm repair was performed before hemodynamic deterioration. The postoperative course was stable, and the patient was discharged without ischemic or procedural complications. CONCLUSIONS This case shows that a previously stable AAA can abruptly destabilize after recent COVID-19. Repeat imaging should be considered when inflammatory markers rise or new symptoms occur, even when symptoms are mild.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. title: Rifampicin-soaked versus bovine prostheses in the management of aortic graft infections: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic vascular graft and endograft infections (aortic VGEI) remain a rare but life-threatening complication following aortic reconstruction. This retrospective study compares outcomes between bovine pericardial graft prostheses and rifampicin-soaked Dacron grafts. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed 62 patients between January 2018 and December 2025 for aortic vascular graft or endograft infection requiring graft explantation and in-situ reconstruction. Patients received either a bovine pericardial graft (n=21) or a rifampicin-soaked Dacron prosthesis (n=41). Survival, treatment failure, perioperative variables, and microbiology were analyzed. RESULTS: Patients in the bovine and rifampicin groups were comparable in terms of age (72.57 vs. 73.58 years, p = 0.685) and sex distribution (85.71% vs. 73.17% male, p = 0.346). BMI, preoperative dialysis, and aortic clamping time were higher in the bovine group. Four treatment failures, defined as persistent or recurrent infection of the reconstructed aortic segment, occurred during follow-up; all were observed after reconstruction with rifampicin-soaked Dacron (4/41, 9.8%), whereas no treatment failure occurred in the bovine pericardial group (0/21). In-hospital mortality was comparable between groups (n=3:14.3% vs. n=8: 19.5%, p = 0.735). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in survival (p = 0.256) or treatment failure rate (p = 0.833). Candida spp. were the most frequent pathogens (27.8%) and significantly associated with secondary aorto-enteric fistula (p=0.003). CONCLUSION: Survival and treatment failure rates were comparable, with a trend toward fewer infection-related complications after bovine pericardial grafting. Despite use in more complex cases, bovine grafts may represent a promising biological alternative.

This retrospective study compares outcomes between bovine pericardial graft prostheses and rifampicin-soaked Dacron grafts. title: Reappraising the safety of menopausal hormone therapy for women-implications for the clinic.
abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) is currently the most effective treatment for vasomotor and other estrogen deficiency-related symptoms. Despite its proven efficacy, concerns regarding long-term safety, particularly breast cancer, venous thromboembolism, and cardiovascular disease, have influenced clinical practice and patterns of MHT use over the past decades. This review summarizes the evolution of evidence regarding the safety of systemic MHT, from the introduction of conjugated equine estrogens in the 1940s through landmark randomized clinical trials to contemporary evidence and international guideline recommendations. Early concerns regarding endometrial safety with estrogen-only treatment were largely resolved by the addition of progestogens for women with an intact uterus. The Women's Health Initiative trial fundamentally changed perceptions of MHT cardiovascular safety, but subsequent analyses established the "timing hypothesis," demonstrating that the benefit-risk profile depends on age and time since menopause at treatment initiation. More recent evidence has highlighted clinically relevant differences between estrogen formulations, routes of administration, and type of progestogen. Transdermal estradiol is associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism than oral estrogen, while micronized progesterone and dydrogesterone may offer a more favorable breast safety profile than some synthetic progestins, although randomized evidence is lacking. Current evidence supports an individualized approach to MHT, with treatment decisions based on symptom burden, age, time since menopause, route of estrogen administration, type of progestogen, and individual risk factors. For healthy women initiating therapy before age 60 years or within 10 years of menopause, the overall benefit-risk profile is favorable. Future research should focus on optimizing formulation-specific safety, generating comparative randomized evidence, and further refining personalized treatment strategies to maximize benefits while minimizing risks.

title: Current Applications of Robotic Surgery in Aortic Procedures: A Scoping Review.
abstract: P P ObjectiveTo map the applications and outcomes of robotic technologies in aortic and aortoiliac procedures, including robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery, endovascular procedures, and micro-robotics.MethodsPubMed was searched up to October 4, 2026, for primary studies including at least 3 patients treated with robotic or robot-assisted interventions for aortic or aortoiliac disease, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Case reports and two-patient series were summarized separately.ResultsFifteen observational studies (552 patients) were included. Robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery (9 studies; 494 patients) was mainly applied to aortoiliac occlusive disease (385 procedures), with robotic proximal aortic anastomosis and open distal anastomoses, and less frequently to aneurysm repair. Conversion rates ranged from 0% to 20%, graft patency from 89% to 100% at up to 48 months, and hospital stay from 4 to 8 days. Robot-assisted endovascular procedures (5 studies; 49 patients) were mostly applied to single procedural steps. Robotic target vessel cannulation succeeded in 81% of vessels, and robotic gate cannulation achieved a shorter catheter path length than manual cannulation (35.7 vs 74.1 cm;= 0.019), but longer cannulation time. Robotic arch navigation was associated with fewer cerebral high-intensity transient signals (median 0 vs 2;= 0.018), and operator radiation dose at the shielded console was 96.5% lower than at the procedure table. No robot-related complications were reported. Micro-robotic sac puncture for type II endoleak embolization (1 study; 9 patients) succeeded in all cases.ConclusionRobotic technologies are a promising and feasible option for selected patients undergoing aortic procedures at experienced centers. Robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery showed acceptable conversion rates and favorable mid-term patency, while endovascular robotics improved technical and surrogate endpoints. As current evidence is limited to small observational series, prospective comparative studies are needed to define the clinical benefit of robotics compared with open and endovascular repair.

title: Secondary Intervention Burden After Fenestrated Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Patient-Level and Procedure-Level Analysis of a 14-Year Single-Center Experience.
abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify the patient-level and procedure-level burden, concentration, timing, and characteristics of secondary interventions after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR), and their association with subsequent mortality. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 189 consecutive patients treated with FEVAR between 2007 and 2021. Secondary interventions were classified by clinical magnitude, approach, timing, and primary indication. The cumulative incidence of a first secondary intervention was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method with death as a competing event. The association with subsequent mortality was assessed using a time-dependent Cox model. RESULTS: P Technical success was achieved in 185 of 189 patients (97.9%). Median observed follow-up was 40.9 months (interquartile range, 25.1-61.2), and median potential follow-up was 57.4 months. Forty-eight patients (25.4%) underwent 67 secondary procedures. Nine patients, representing 4.8% of the cohort, underwent repeated interventions and accounted for 28 procedures (41.8%). Of the 67 procedures, 25 (37.3%) were major, 42 (62.7%) were minor, and 52 (77.6%) were endovascular. Thirty-seven procedures (55.2%) occurred more than 1 year after FEVAR. The 48-month cumulative incidence of a first secondary intervention was 24.7%, compared with 27.0% using 1 minus Kaplan-Meier. At the last available imaging examination, 610 of 615 assessable fenestrated target vessels were patent (99.2%). Secondary intervention was not statistically associated with subsequent mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.11; 95% confidence interval, 0.68-1.80; = .687). CONCLUSION: Secondary interventions affected approximately one quarter of patients after FEVAR, but a small subgroup accounted for a disproportionate share of the procedural burden. Most procedures were minor and endovascular, and more than half occurred beyond 1 year. No statistically significant average association with subsequent mortality was identified. Reporting both patient- and procedure-level burden may better characterize FEVAR durability and follow-up requirements.Clinical ImpactSecondary interventions after fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) are commonly reported as the proportion of patients undergoing at least 1 procedure, which does not capture cumulative procedural burden. In this cohort of 189 patients, 48 underwent 67 secondary interventions, whereas only 9 patients, representing 4.8% of the cohort, accounted for 41.8% of all procedures. Most interventions were minor and endovascular, but more than half occurred beyond 1 year. These findings indicate that first reintervention rates alone incompletely describe FEVAR durability. Reporting both patient- and procedure-level burden may better inform patient counseling, surveillance planning, and comparisons across devices and centers by highlighting the concentration of procedures in a small subgroup.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 189 consecutive patients treated with FEVAR between 2007 and 2021. Secondary interventions were classified by clinical magnitude, approach, timing, and primary indication.

title: Evaluation of morphometric characteristics and positional variations of the carotid sinus using computed tomography angiography.
abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to determine the morphometric characteristics and spatial variations of the carotid sinus (CS) using computed tomography angiography (CTA) images. METHODS: In the study, cervical CTA images of a total of 100 individuals (200 sides) comprising 55 men and 45 women were examined. The diameters of the proximal and distal segments of the common carotid artery (CCA) and the internal carotid artery (ICA), as well as the proximal diameter of the external carotid artery (ECA), were measured. In addition, measurements of the maximum transverse diameter and length of the CS were taken; the resulting data were compared according to the variables of age, gender and side. RESULTS: All artery diameters, CS length (mean 8.78 ± 1.33 mm), and maximum CS diameter (mean 8.27 ± 1.10 mm) were found to be significantly higher in men than in women (p < 0.001). It was determined that the diameters of the CCA and ICA on the left side were statistically significantly wider than those on the right side (p < 0.001). It was found that CS localization was asymmetric in 29% of cases and most commonly occurred in the proximal ICA (Type I) in 74.5% of cases. In addition, a positive and statistically significant correlation (r = 0.554; p < 0.001) was found between age and CS length. CONCLUSION: Understanding the morphological variations of the CS is of critical importance in preventing unintended CS stimulation and related complications during surgical procedures in this region, particularly carotid endarterectomy.

title: L5 Corpectomy in a 12-Year-Old Owing to Rosai-Dorfman Disease: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis typically presenting with massive, painless lymphadenopathy or subcutaneous masses. Extranodal involvement, particularly in the spine, is exceedingly rare and poses significant diagnostic and management challenges. Lumbar spinal RDD with vertebral collapse and neurological compromise is almost unheard of in the pediatric population, with no prior reports of surgical intervention requiring L5 corpectomy and circumferential fusion in an adolescent. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present a case of a 12-year-old girl with a 6-month history of worsening lower back pain unresponsive to conservative treatment. Imaging revealed collapse of the L5 vertebral body and a destructive, enhancing lesion encasing the neural elements, leading to severe canal and foraminal stenosis. Computed tomography-guided biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of RDD. A multidisciplinary surgical team implemented a 2-stage circumferential surgical plan. Stage 1 involved posterior decompression and posterior instrumentation from L3 to the pelvis using S2AI screws. A silastic barrier was placed to protect neural elements. Stage 2, performed via an anterior approach with vascular surgery assistance, involved complete corpectomy of L5 and reconstruction with an expandable cage spanning L4 to S1. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient remained neurologically intact. At 1-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated solid anterior and posterior fusion, maintained spinal alignment, and had returned to full activity. CONCLUSION: This is the first reported case of pediatric RDD requiring an L5 corpectomy with circumferential spinal fusion. The case underscores the importance of early tissue diagnosis, individualized surgical planning, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Recognition of RDD as a potential etiology for pediatric spinal lesions is critical, particularly when imaging mimics malignancy. Our successful outcome supports the use of staged, tailored surgical approaches in managing rare spinal pathologies in children.

title: Comparative Safety and Efficacy of Apixaban and Rivaroxaban During Extended Anticoagulation for Venous Thromboembolism: A Non-randomised Post Hoc Comparison Within the RENOVE Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Some evidence reported that rivaroxaban use is associated with a higher risk of clinically relevant bleeding (CRB) than apixaban during the first months of treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE). We aimed to determine whether the risk of CRB is higher with rivaroxaban than apixaban during extended treatment, either at full or reduced dose. METHODS: versus The RENOVE open-label randomised controlled trial compared full-dosereduced-dose of apixaban or rivaroxaban in patients who had completed at least 6 months of full-dose treatment for VTE and required extended anticoagulation. Drug choice was not randomised. In this post-analysis, the primary outcome was centrally-adjudicated CRB events. Treatment effects were estimated using crude hazard ratio (HR), adjusted HR, and an inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). RESULTS: versus versus IPTW IPTW Among 2768 enrolled patients, 1513 received rivaroxaban (755 full-dose, 758 reduced-dose) and 1255 apixaban (630 full-dose, 625 reduced-dose). Median age was 62.666.5 years and proportion of female was 32.1%38.7%, respectively. Median follow-up was 37 months. The 5-year cumulative incidence of CRB was 11.7% with rivaroxaban and 13.7% with apixaban (adjusted-HR 0.90 [95%CI 0.70-1.17], HR0.92 [0.70-1.21]). The incidence of major bleeding, recurrent VTE, composite outcome, arterial thromboembolic events, and all-cause death were similar. Serious adverse event not related to VTE and CRB was 7.7% and 10.8%, respectively (adjusted-HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.57-0.97], HR0.76 [0.55-1.04]). CONCLUSIONS: During extended anticoagulation, no difference in clinically relevant bleeding or recurrent VTE was observed between rivaroxaban and apixaban, although that non-randomised treatment allocation possibly influenced outcomes.

title: Cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks of sex hormone therapy: from contraception to transgender care.
abstract: The risk of venous thromboembolism is increased with combined oral contraceptives, rises with the dose of ethinylestradiol, and is higher with desogestrel, gestodene, drospirenone or cyproterone acetate than with levonorgestrel; the determinant is not the generation of the pill but the residual androgen-receptor activity of the progestin, which modulates the hepatic effect of the estrogen. Age over 35 years, obesity, smoking and a family history of thrombosis amplify it. Pills based on a native estrogen have a more limited hepatic impact and rank below most ethinylestradiol combinations in contemporary cohorts, but their clinical safety is not demonstrated and no comparative outcome data exist for estetrol/drospirenone. Androgenicity is not a general marker of venous safety: injectable depot medroxyprogesterone acetate, given alone at supraphysiological doses, carries an increased risk. Myocardial infarction and stroke are also more frequent, but against a very low background - about 21 additional strokes and 10 additional infarctions per 100,000 person-years, four times fewer than the venous excess - and, unlike venous events, independent of progestin type. Menopause hormone therapy increases venous thromboembolic risk, especially in the first year; the route of administration is the main determinant, transdermal estradiol with micronized progesterone appearing safest. In cisgender men, testosterone deficiency carries increased cardiovascular risk, and randomized and real-world data support the safety of transdermal replacement, although more pulmonary embolism and atrial fibrillation have been observed. In trans women, observational data show an increased risk of stroke and venous thromboembolism, particularly with oral estradiol and cyproterone acetate, whereas recent large-scale data show no excess of major cardiovascular events with testosterone in trans men. The practical consequences are specific: no combined pill is acceptable after a venous thromboembolic event, with a thrombogenic mutation or with migraine with aura, native-estrogen pills included; transdermal estradiol should be preferred for menopause and feminising hormone therapy; and haematocrit should guide the dose and route of testosterone.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with REML estimation of between-study variance (ORs); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI). RESULTS: Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (8 studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%. CONCLUSIONS: In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.

title: Acute Limb Ischemia: Medicare and Medicaid Reimbursement Gaps Threaten Sustainability of Care.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a vascular emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and substantial resource utilization. However, contemporary data evaluating the financial sustainability of ALI care across insurance types remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate hospitalization costs, reimbursement, profitability, and contribution margin for operative ALI care stratified by insurance status and revascularization strategy. METHODS: A retrospective review of patients admitted with ALI at a quaternary medical center (2016-2024) was performed. Patients were identified using ICD-10 and CPT codes. Exclusion criteria were outpatient encounters and non-operative or non-procedural management. Hospitalization cost was defined as the sum of variable and fixed costs. Profit was reimbursement minus cost. Analyses were stratified by insurance status and treatment modality. Continuous variables were compared using nonparametric tests, with statistical significance set at p<0.05. RESULTS: A total of 565 patients were included, of whom 60.2% were insured by Medicare, 24.2% by Medicaid, and 15.6% by commercial insurance. Median total hospitalization costs exceeded $50,000 per admission and did not differ by insurance status (Medicare $50,894 [IQR $33,496-$90,923], Medicaid $49,417 [$33,775-$83,379], commercial $56,603 [$35,823-$96,067]; p=0.577) or by revascularization strategy (open vs endovascular; p>0.05). Professional and technical cost components were similarly comparable across payer groups. Despite similar costs, reimbursement varied significantly by insurance status. Medicare and Medicaid admissions were associated with median hospital losses of -$12,673 [-$28,732 to -$1,425] and -$3,176 [-$10,035 to $3,859], respectively, while commercially insured admissions generated a median profit of $30,622 [$7,602-$50,208] (p<0.001). These differences persisted across both open and endovascular subgroups. CONCLUSION: Operative management of ALI is associated with substantial hospitalization costs that are consistent across revascularization strategies and payer types. While commercially insured admissions generated positive contribution margins, Medicare and Medicaid reimbursements were insufficient to offset costs. Given that most patients were insured through Medicare, the reimbursement disparities translated into an overall negative financial impact for ALI care. Without reimbursement reform or payment adjustment, the long-term financial sustainability of ALI care, and equitable patient access to timely revascularization, may be jeopardized.

title: A Vascular Surgery and Primary Care Partnership for Improving Resident Training in Peripheral Artery Disease Management.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early diagnosis, establishment of best medical management, and timely specialty referral for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain ongoing challenges. In this study, we sought to identify gaps in internal medicine (IM) and family medicine (FM) residents' self-rated competency of PAD management and investigated whether an educational session led by vascular surgeons could promote recognition and confidence in patient care. STUDY DESIGN: A single educational session, featuring a PowerPoint presentation, hands-on training (pulse and Doppler examination), and open discussion, was offered to IM and FM residents on two separate occasions. A pre-session survey assessed self-rated knowledge, practices, attitudes, and medical training regarding PAD, followed by a truncated post-session survey. The responses were grouped as high vs. moderate/low. Descriptive statistics and the McNemar Exact test were used for paired sample comparison. RESULTS: Thirty-one residents completed both surveys (65% IM, 35% FM, 58% male, and 77% first- or second-year trainees). Pre-session data revealed gaps in knowledge with few residents rating their understanding as "high." Post-session, there was a significant increase across all measured areas (p<0.001). Notably, improvements were seen in the number of residents who felt highly confident in diagnosing PAD (from 16.1% to 90.3%), using a vascular Doppler (6.5% to 83.9%), ordering non-invasive testing (from 6.5% to 83.9%), performing a lower extremity pulse exam (from 12.9% to 87.1%), managing PAD for amputation prevention (from 12.9% to 71.0%), and referring to a vascular specialist (from 25.8% to 83.9%). CONCLUSION: Resident knowledge and confidence improved significantly as a result of a singular educational session. This collaborative model between vascular surgery educators and primary care residency programs demonstrates an adaptable framework that successfully addresses a gap in PAD management training.

title: Chronic thoracic aortitis versus primary medial degeneration in ascending aorta: a digital morphometric analysis of aortic layers remodelling.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic aortitis (CA) represents a diverse group of inflammatory conditions often diagnosed incidentally in ascending aorta biopsies. While the 2015 and 2016 Consensus Statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta provide standardised histological classifications, data quantifying structural remodelling within individual aortic layers remain limited. Furthermore, distinguishing CA from primary non-inflammatory medial degeneration (MD) can be challenging, particularly when inflammation is sparse or burnt out, and secondary degenerative changes predominate. We aimed to compare morphological changes in CA and MD aneurysms and apply digital image analysis to quantify aortic wall layers. METHODS: Retrospective histological analysis was performed on 63 ascending aortic specimens: CA (n=21), MD (n=21), and autopsy controls (n=21). Digitised elastic-stained sections were analysed using QuPath software to measure the thickness and cross-sectional area of the intima (I), media (M), and adventitia (A). Overall MD scores (i.e., summaries of each MD grade component) were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis based on binary logistic regression models. RESULTS: CA demonstrated a profound architectural shift, characterised by medial thinning alongside marked intimal and adventitial expansion, resulting in significantly lower M/(I+A) thickness and area ratios compared with MD and controls (p <0.001). CA specimens also exhibited the most severe secondary degenerative changes, with significantly higher overall MD scores (median: 15 vs. 8; p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis revealed diagnostic utility of both the M/(I+A) thickness ratio (AUC = 0.964) and the M/(I+A) area ratio (AUC = 0.955) for identifying CA. A multivariable model combining the overall MD score with the M/(I+A) thickness ratio achieved an AUC of 0.971 (accuracy 88.1%), whereas combining it with the M/(I+A) area ratio yielded an AUC of 0.968 (accuracy 90.5%). CONCLUSION: Digital morphometric analysis provides a reproducible and feasible method for quantifying structural remodelling in chronic aortitis. Changes in the proportions of the aortic layers, specifically intimal and adventitial expansion combined with medial thinning and severe secondary medial degeneration, can facilitate accurate differentiation of aortic wall pathologies, particularly in cases with sparse inflammation.

title: Calibrated Microspheres versus Liquid Embolic Agents for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Single-Center Clinicoradiologic Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAe) is an effective treatment for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), but the optimal embolic agent remains debated. Landmark randomized trials predominantly used liquid embolics, although calibrated microspheres remain widely used. We compared clinicoradiologic outcomes after MMAe with 75 μm Embozene microspheres versus liquid embolics (n-butyl cyanoacrylate or Onyx 18). METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed single-agent MMAe for cSDH at a tertiary center (January 2019-January 2025). The embolized MMA was the unit of analysis; agent choice was discretionary. The efficacy cohort required 2-8 week imaging (n = 66); the safety cohort included all single-agent procedures (n = 67; 35 particle, 32 liquid). Primary outcomes were embolization failure and unplanned surgical evacuation. Secondary outcomes included early SDH thickness, midline shift, and latest modified Rankin scale (mRS). RESULTS: Fifty patients underwent 66 embolizations (16 bilateral): 34 particle and 32 liquid. Embolization failure occurred in 5/34 versus 4/32, and unplanned evacuation in 3/34 versus 1/32; events were few and the comparison underpowered. Female patients were more frequent in the particle group (47% vs 19%, P = 0.020). Early SDH thickness was 8 (6) versus 6 (6) mm (P = 0.340). The safety cohort had one fatal posterior-circulation infarct after Embozene (1/35 vs 0/32) and no other periprocedural complications. CONCLUSION: Embolization failure was similar between 75 μm Embozene and liquid embolics, while unplanned evacuation was numerically higher with particles. Given infrequent events, limited sample size, and baseline imbalances, agent selection may be individualized by anatomy, visualization, and operator experience.

title: Effect of Microvascular Disease on Re-amputation Risk after Unilateral Amputation due to Diabetes or Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between manifestations of microvascular disease (MVD) and other factors on re-amputation risk within 12 months following incident unilateral lower extremity amputation. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 8 924 patients with first unilateral transmetatarsal, transtibial, or transfemoral amputation secondary to diabetes and or peripheral arterial disease, identified through a Veterans Affairs database. Re-amputation was defined as any subsequent ipsilateral soft tissue or bony revision or amputation to a higher level. The presence of MVD was determined using a composite variable that required the involvement of each subcomponent (neuropathy, nephropathy, and retinopathy), and also by evaluating each of the subcomponent MVD variables separately. Twenty-nine additional risk factors were evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of re-amputation. A competing risk analysis estimated the cumulative incidence of re-amputation. The effect of risk factors on re-amputation risk was estimated by computing subdistribution hazard ratios (sub-HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: The twelve month re-amputation risk was 38.0% (transmetatarsal), 27.2% (transtibial), and 14.1% (transfemoral). The combined MVD variable was not significantly associated with re-amputation risk. However, re-amputation after transmetatarsal amputation was significantly elevated in patients with retinopathy, leukocytosis, or those who were on kidney dialysis, with the highest risk in those with all three (sub-HR 2.2, 95% CI 1.8 - 2.6). Similarly, for transtibial patients, the risk was higher in the presence of retinopathy, leukocytosis, and kidney dialysis, and in those with a prior ipsilateral revascularisation and those on warfarin. The highest risk was observed in those with all factors present (sub-HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.6 - 2.7). CONCLUSION: This study identified an important association between the pre-amputation diagnosis of retinopathy and risk for subsequent failure of primary healing and need for re-amputation. Presence of retinopathy should be considered when evaluating potential failure of healing during amputation level decisions.

title: Outcomes of Total Endovascular Repair of Aortic Arch and Thoraco-abdominal Aortic Aneurysms in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group in a Selected Group of Patients with Extensive Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to report outcomes of total endovascular aortic repair (TEAR) using arch branched endovascular aortic repair (aBEVAR) and thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR). METHODS: Clinical data from 16 participating centres in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively analysed. All patients who underwent TEAR were included. The primary outcome was aortic related mortality (ARM). Secondary outcomes included stroke and or transient ischaemic attack (TIA), spinal cord ischaemia (SCI), and freedom from target artery (TA) instability, re-interventions, and new cardiovascular events (CVEs) within 1 year. RESULTS: Of 98 patients scheduled for TEAR, 95 (97%) completed both stages, including 46 (48%) with chronic post-dissection aneurysms and 49 (52%) with degenerative aneurysms. A multistage approach with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was used in all patients, with a median interval between stages of 11 months (interquartile range [IQR] 5, 14). One (1%) rupture occurred between the staged procedures (successfully managed with off the shelf TAAA multibranch stent graft). Custom made and off the shelf TAAA FBEVAR devices were used in 79 (83%) and 16 (17%) patients, respectively. There were 12 (13%) stroke and or TIAs (aBEVAR, ten; TAAA FBEVAR, two); five (5%) had a modified Rankin Scale score > 3. Sixteen patients (17%) experienced SCI (aBEVAR, two; TAAA FBEVAR, 14) with three cases (3%) of paraplegia. Four patients (4%) died within thirty days; these were the only cases of ARM. Median follow up was 32 months (IQR 3, 61). Of 67 patients (71%) with available one year follow up, there were six (9%) with TA instability and five (7%) CVEs. Estimated three year survival was 79 ± 5% with a cumulative incidence of re-intervention of 31 ± 6%. CONCLUSION: Multistage TEAR with aBEVAR followed by TAAA FBEVAR was associated with low ARM, re-intervention, and TA instability. Stroke and SCI remain significant and must be carefully weighed during patient selection and treatment.

METHODS: Clinical data from 16 participating centres in the International Multicenter Aortic Research Group from 2014 to 2024 were retrospectively analysed. All patients who underwent TEAR were included.

title: Sepsis Prior to Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Elevated Rates of Myocardial Infarction and Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients who have sepsis often experience persistent physiological instability, which may increase vulnerability to postoperative complications. However, the impact of preoperative sepsis on outcomes following elective total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains poorly defined. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate the association of preoperative sepsis with 90-day and two-year postoperative complications following TKA. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted utilizing an insurance database. Patients who had a preoperative diagnosis of sepsis within two years prior to TKA were matched 1:3 to controls based on demographics and comorbidities. Patients who had sepsis were stratified according to the following timeline: sepsis three months prior to surgery, three to six months prior, six to 12 months prior, 12 to 18 months prior, and 18 to 24 months prior. Medical and surgical complications were assessed at 90 days and two years following surgery. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Patients who had sepsis within two years prior to surgery exhibited increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) (odds ratio (OR): 1.6), postoperative sepsis (OR: 2.7), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.4), urinary tract infection (OR: 1.8), blood transfusion (OR: 2.0), readmission (OR: 1.3), and wound dehiscence (OR: 1.4) within 90 days of surgery. At two years following surgery, sepsis was associated with elevated rates of revision surgery (OR: 1.3), PJI (OR: 1.6), osteomyelitis (OR: 1.9), and mortality (OR: 1.3). Sepsis within three months of operation was associated with elevated rates of myocardial infarction (OR: 2.1) and deep vein thrombosis (OR: 2.0). All findings were statistically significant at P < 0.05. CONCLUSION: Preoperative sepsis is associated with increased complications following TKA, including periprosthetic joint infection and mortality. Sepsis within three months of surgery confers a particularly elevated risk of myocardial infarction and deep vein thrombosis following TKA.

title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
abstract: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.

Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors.

title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.

title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF). METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory. RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation.

title: Making vascular outcomes visible: an implementation framework for an Irish national vascular registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ireland lacks a coordinated national vascular registry, despite a 2023 National Model of Care recommendation to establish one for quality improvement and implant surveillance. AIMS: To identify transferable features of established national vascular registry and audit systems and translate them into a proportionate implementation framework for Ireland. METHODS: A structured narrative review and comparative implementation analysis. Five mature comparator systems, purposively selected for relevance to predefined implementation domains, were characterised using contemporary programme documentation and targeted peer-reviewed literature. Features were mapped to Irish policy objectives. RESULTS: Transferable functions included explicit measurement of case ascertainment, clinically granular procedure-specific modules, recurrent provider feedback, linkage to routinely collected data, and progressive development of risk-adjusted benchmarking and research capability. We propose an Irish registry beginning with infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, carotid intervention, lower-limb arterial revascularisation, and major amputation. The initial architecture should combine a limited universal clinical core with procedure-specific modules, reconciliation against Hospital In-Patient Enquiry activity, structured implant capture, and rapid feedback to participating centres. Procedure-specific risk adjustment, longitudinal linkage, complex aortic modules, and participation in VASCUNET should follow only after completeness and data quality are established. Prospective pilot evaluation should measure denominator validity, case ascertainment, mandatory-field completion, data-entry burden, provider acceptability, staffing requirements, and cost per completed case. CONCLUSIONS: Ireland does not require further proof that national vascular audit is feasible; it requires a deliberately limited, testable, and sustainably commissioned implementation model.

AIMS: To identify transferable features of established national vascular registry and audit systems and translate them into a proportionate implementation framework for Ireland. METHODS: A structured narrative review and comparative implementation analysis.
