title: Anesthetic technique is associated with complication risk and healthcare utilization following total shoulder arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: Compare perioperative complications and healthcare utilization among total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) patients receiving general (GA), regional (RA), or combined anesthesia (RA + GA). METHODS: Using the TriNetX database, patients undergoing primary TSA were identified and stratified into three groups based on anesthetic technique: GA, RA, and combined RA + GA. 1:1 Propensity score matching was performed to using the GA cohort as reference to control for baseline demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes of interest included 90-day complication rates including UTI, venous thromboembolism (VTE), acute kidney injury (AKI), prosthetic joint infection (PJI), pneumonia, constipation, and revision TSA, emergency department (ED) visits and hospital readmission, Foley catheter insertion, postoperative opioid prescriptions and mean opioid number of prescriptions. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: Comparing GA with RA, each cohort consisted of 28,564 patients. RA was associated with lower rates of UTI, AKI, constipation, pneumonia, fewer patients prescribed opioids and fewer opioid prescriptions per patient while being associated with increased healthcare utilization compared to GA alone. Comparing RA + GA with GA alone, 17,926 matched patients were included in each cohort. RA + GA was associated with lower rates of UTI and opioid prescriptions, and higher rates of healthcare utilization compared to GA alone. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that while RA provides early analgesic and opioid-sparing benefits after TSA, it is associated with increased post-operative healthcare utilization. These findings help guide surgical decision making and highlight the need for standardized perioperative protocols to optimize postoperative pain control and manage rebound pain-related care utilization with RA techniques. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

title: Exploratory topological modeling of reported frequencies of aortic arch branching variations.
abstract: Anatomical variations in the branching patterns of the aortic arch affect endovascular access, surgical planning, and cerebral perfusion strategies. However, the quantitative relationship between branching topology and the frequency distribution of these variations remains unclear. The study aimed to explore whether topological differences among final aortic arch branching configurations are associated with their reported frequencies. Seven pooled type-level frequency estimates from a published meta-analysis were analyzed. Node-Shift and Edge-Loss-Change Scores were defined from the final branching topology relative to Type 1 (separate brachiocephalic, left common carotid, and left subclavian origins from a left-sided arch). A three-parameter log-linear model was fitted by ordinary least squares to natural-log-transformed frequencies. Leave-one-out cross-validation and sensitivity analyses by study modality, study size, and exclusion of Type 1 or Type 4 (common brachiocephalic-left common carotid origin with a left vertebral artery arising directly from the arch) were performed. The fitted log-linear model had an intercept of 4.491 and coefficients of -2.751 for the Node-Shift Score and - 5.474 for the Edge-Loss-Change Score. The coefficient of determination was 0.932 on the log-frequency scale and 0.974 after back-transformation to the original frequency scale. Leave-one-out Q² values were 0.821 and 0.778 on the log and original scales, respectively. Coefficients remained negative in imaging-only, cadaveric-only, studies with at least 100 specimens, Type 1-excluded, and Type 4-excluded analyses. Within this seven-type aggregated dataset, configurations with larger topological scores had lower reported frequencies. The proposed scores provide a compact exploratory description of branching variation, but the model does not establish a developmental mechanism, predict individual anatomy, or support direct clinical decision-making without external validation.

However, the quantitative relationship between branching topology and the frequency distribution of these variations remains unclear. The study aimed to explore whether topological differences among final aortic arch branching configurations are associated with their reported frequencies.

title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening. METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model. RESULTS: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such. CONCLUSIONS: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.

title: Artificial intelligence in varicose veins: Comparative insights from other vascular diseases, evidence gaps, and future prospects.
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in varicose veins (VV), covering applications in image recognition, postoperative management, risk factor and biomarker analysis, and the use of large language models (LLMs) to aid clinical decision-making. While significant advancements have been made, valuable lessons can be drawn from AI applications in other vascular diseases. Key considerations for advancing AI in VV include ensuring methodological rigor, high quality data, external validation, strict attention to data security and legal standards, and linking AI tools to clinically important outcomes. It is recommended that machine learning models be developed and validated within standardized frameworks that future VV research can adopt. Accordingly, the development of clear guidelines and benchmarks is imperative. LLMs hold promise in relieving clinicians of repetitive routine tasks, thereby enhancing diagnostic accuracy and assisting in treatment planning. Additionally, LLM-based tools could support the curation of medical content on short video platforms and assist clinicians in creating educational materials, ultimately improving patient engagement and understanding.

title: ® ® Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus ZilverPTXin treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
abstract: Aim: Materials & methods: Results: Conclusion: ® ® To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus ZilverPTXdrug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database.This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI.A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup.Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

title: Continuity of Chronic Wound Care Across Hospital-to-Home Transitions: A Qualitative Study of Hospital and Community Nurses' Experiences.
abstract: AimTo explore how hospital nurses (HNs) and community nurses (CNs) in France manage chronic wound care for older adults across settings, and how their practices shape continuity of care during hospital-to-home transitions.DesignQualitative descriptive study combining ethnographic shadowing and a focus group.MethodsFieldwork took place in a French university hospital, across four units: acute geriatrics, rehabilitation, vascular surgery, dermatology. The focus group involved CNs from seven different self-employed nursing practices. We shadowed 15 HNs for approximately 92 h and conducted one focus group with 7 CNs. Data were analyzed inductively using constant comparison, with a second-stage interpretive analysis informed by Meleis' transitions theory.ResultsFour interconnected processes shaped continuity of chronic wound care across the transition: (1) nursing expertise in wound management was expressed differently across hospital and community settings; (2) discharge coordination was fragmented, with rare nurse-to-nurse communication and insufficient transfer of wound-specific information; (3) organizational logics diverged, with discontinuous hospital workflows and time-pressured, fee-for-service-constrained community visits; and (4) patient involvement during hospitalization was limited, constraining engagement and preparedness post-discharge. Continuity was frequently maintained through compensatory work from nurses.ConclusionContinuity of chronic wound care depends less on nursing expertise than on the organizational conditions enabling that expertise to be mobilized across settings.ImpactThis study highlights the need for more integrated transitional care, including clearer and more consistent responsibilities at discharge, structured nurse-to-nurse discharge communication, and earlier patient involvement in wound care management.

title: Prostatic Artery Embolization in a Patient With Bilateral Internal Iliac Artery Occlusions.
abstract: Background: Study Sample: Results: Conclusions: Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is an established treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia but can be challenging in complex anatomy.An 86-year-old male with history of abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and aortobifemoral bypass presented with gross hematuria and urinary retention. Imaging and clinical evaluation confirmed BPH-related clot retention as the etiology. Careful review of preprocedural CT angiography revealed occluded bilateral internal iliac arteries, a right aberrant obturator artery (AOA) (corona mortis variant), arising from the inferior epigastric artery, which itself originated from the native right external iliac artery. The AOA supplied the entire prostate, perfusing both lobes and contributing to the contralateral pelvic circulation as well. Cone-beam CT and angiography confirmed the perfusion to both prostatic lobes. PAE was performed by accessing the native common femoral artery and selectively catheterizing the AOA. Embolization of the prostatic parenchyma was completed successfully while preserving flow to adjacent pelvic structures, avoiding non-target embolization.The patient had complete resolution of hematuria and urinary retention and remained catheter-free at 1-year follow-up.This case highlights the importance of pre-procedural evaluation and planning, demonstrating that PAE can be safely and effectively performed even in variant vascular anatomy.

title: Use of a central venous catheter as vascular access at the start of a regular hemodialysis program: impact on mortality over 2 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The recommended access for starting chronic hemodialysis (HD) is an arteriovenous fistula (AVF), but a (CVC) continues to be frequently used. Worldwide, its use has been associated with higher mortality, but data from Brazil are lacking. METHODS: Analytical, observational, and retrospective cohort study that aimed at analyzing the data available in the Brazilian Monthly Dialysis Registry database from Jan/2011 to Dec/2023. Using data from this registry, we evaluated the frequency of CVC use (regardless of whether tunneled or non-tunneled) at the start of HD across 13 years and assessed its impact on all-cause mortality over 2 years. RESULTS: We studied 10,182 patients. The mean age was 59 (47-69) years; 59% were male, and 33% had diabetes. CVC use at HD entry increased substantially in the last 10 years. The 2-year mortality rates for CVC and primary AVF/graft users were 20% and 9%, respectively, P < 0.001. In the fully adjusted multivariate model, the use of CVC persisted significantly associated with mortality (HR 1.69, 95%CI 1.23-2.25, P=0.001). Other variables directly associated with mortality were age (HR 1.04, 95%CI 1.03-1.05, P=0.001), and serum ferritin (HR 1.18, 95%CI 1.06-1.30, P=0.002). Serum albumin (HR 0.86, 95%CI 0.84-0.88, P<0.001) and URR (HR 0.97, 95%CI 0.96-0.97, P<0.001) emerged as protective factors. CONCLUSIONS: CVC use was associated with a 1.69-fold increased risk of 2-year mortality. The increasing use of CVCs in Brazil is concerning and highlights the need for public health strategies promoting timely permanent vascular access before HD initiation.

title: Ultrasound-guided cyanoacrylate embolization of refluxing tributaries during truncal cyanoacrylate closure (SLICE): Technique description and a proof-of-concept feasibility study.
abstract: p ObjectivesTruncal cyanoacrylate closure (CAC) does not treat refluxing tributary varicosities. We describe Side-branch Local Injection of Cyanoacrylate Embolization (SLICE) - ultrasound-guided injection of the VenaSeal adhesive into refluxing tributaries during truncal CAC - and assess its technical feasibility and periprocedural safety.MethodsSingle-center retrospective review of 32 consecutive patients (49 limbs, 58 truncal veins) treated by truncal CAC between September 2024 and December 2025; SLICE was performed in 14. The primary endpoint was technical success, defined as the absence of reflux within an injected tributary on the first postoperative duplex study. Secondary endpoints included 3-month durability, truncal occlusion, and adverse events.Results22 refluxing tributaries were injected; all were epifascial, at a median depth of 4.0 mm (range 1.2-9.6). A median of four dispenser trigger pulls was used per site (range 3-8); the series was underpowered to relate pull count to diameter (Spearman rho -0.16,= 0.50). Technical success was 21/22 (95%; 95% confidence interval 77.2-99.9) initially and 19/20 (95%; 75.1-99.9) at 3 months. On 3-month computed tomography (CT), 14 of 17 evaluable injected tributaries were occluded whereas 16 of 17 were free of reflux: anatomical occlusion lagged behind hemodynamic success. Truncal occlusion was preserved (30/30 at 1 week; 26/27 at 3 months). There was no phlebitis, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or adhesive removal. Hyperpigmentation occurred in 3/14 patients, all with an injection <2 mm below the skin; two mild delayed hypersensitivity reactions occurred, both over the truncal rather than an injected site. One patient (7%) required re-intervention.ConclusionsSLICE is technically feasible and reproducible within a narrow range of adhesive delivery, with no adhesive-related complication at an injected site in this small series with short follow-up. Prospective comparative evaluation with patient-centered endpoints is required before efficacy can be claimed.

title: Electrosurgical septotomy across the full spectrum of aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. METHODS: Retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < 0.001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital and overall mortality were 10%, 14% and 19%, with one fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.

title: Adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection incidence and mortality: results from the UK Biobank, the J-SHC study and a meta-analysis of cohort studies.
abstract: trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend 2 2 2 2 Few studies have investigated the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection and data is lacking on adiposity measures other than body mass index (BMI). We analyzed the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection in the UK Biobank, and the Japan Specific Health Checkups (J-SHC) Study, and conducted a meta-analysis of cohort studies to clarify the associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. The analytical cohorts included 496,255 participants in the UK Biobank and 630,841 participants in the J-SHC Study. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. PubMed and Embase were searched for relevant studies up to February 27, 2026. Random effects models were used to calculate summary relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. In the UK Biobank and J-SHC, there were 371 and 105 aortic dissections during 12.3 and 4 years follow-up, respectively. In the UK Biobank, positive associations (HRs, 95% CIs) were observed between high BMI (1.54, 1.01-2.37, p=0.01), waist circumference (1.82, 1.27-2.60, p=0.001), hip circumference (1.77, 1.25-2.50, p<0.001), waist-to-height ratio (1.88, 1.30-2.70, p=0.10), and fat mass (1.36, 0.97-1.91, p=0.02) and aortic dissection risk, but no clear association was observed for waist-to-hip ratio (1.28, 0.90-1.81, p=0.08) and body fat percentage (1.09, 0.77-1.54, p=0.53). In the J-SHC Study, higher BMI (2.36, 0.98-4.84, p=0.018), waist circumference (2.26, 1.18-4.60, p=0.003), and waist-to-height ratio (2.61, 1.27-5.92, p=0.009) were positively associated with aortic dissection mortality. Five cohort studies were included in the meta-analysis on BMI and aortic dissection (2007 cases and 4,962,288 participants). The summary RR per 5 kg/mincrement in BMI was 1.09 (1.00-1.20, I = 43%), per 10 cm increment in waist circumference was 1.21 (1.05-1.40, I = 50%, n = 2), and per 0.1 unit increment in waist-to-height ratio was 1.32 (1.08-1.61, I = 39%, n = 2). These findings provide evidence for a positive association between both general and abdominal adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection, with the strongest associations observed for high waist-to-height ratio. Although further large-scale studies are warranted for confirmation, these findings suggest avoiding excess weight may be an important strategy for the prevention of aortic dissection.

title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: p At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025.

title: Probable Loeys-Dietz Syndrome with aortic root dilatation and multiple arterial tortuosity in resource-limited setting : A case report.
abstract: Loeys-Dietz Syndrome (LDS) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder that is characterized by multisystem disorders predisposing individuals to arterial and aortic aneurysms. We present the case of a 17-year-old Bangladeshi male referred to cardiology for assessment of systemic abnormalities and cardiovascular risk. He presented with craniofacial, musculoskeletal, and cutaneous abnormalities including hypertelorism, mandibular ectopic hair, joint hypermobility with mild thoracic scoliosis, residual talipes equinovarus. He had past medical history of surgically corrected congenital anomalies. Based on clinical and radiological findings, he was diagnosed with clinically suspected Loeys-Dietz Syndrome as genetic testing was unavailable. He was managed through a multidisciplinary approach with regular follow-up. This report adds to literature on Loeys-Dietz Syndrome, emphasizing on aortic root dilatation and carotid artery tortuosity as important clinical and radiological features supporting diagnosis of LDS particularly in young patients presenting with characteristic craniofacial abnormalities or suggestive radiological findings. Early recognition and multidisciplinary management are crucial in resource-limited settings to prevent life-threatening vascular complications.

title: Age-dependent impact of diabetes on limb events and mortality in patients with peripheral artery disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial risks of limb events and mortality. Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear. METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026). Patients were stratified by diabetes status and age at PAD diagnosis (35-50 vs > 50 years). The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-extremity revascularization or major amputation. All-cause mortality was a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, interaction analyses, and propensity score overlap weighting were performed. RESULTS: P P P P Among 4538 patients aged 35-50 years at PAD diagnosis, 1902 (42%) had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 12.0 years, diabetes was independently associated with higher risks of MALE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-2.01,= .032) and mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.70,< .001). Diabetes was associated with increased MALE risk in both age groups, with no significant interaction by age (for interaction = .498). In contrast, the association between diabetes and mortality was significantly stronger in patients aged 35-50 years than in those aged >50 years (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.72-2.33 vs 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33,for interaction < .001). Excess mortality associated with diabetes emerged during longer-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with increased risks of MALE and mortality in PAD, with a stronger association with mortality among patients diagnosed before age 50. These findings identify diabetes as a marker of particularly high risk in premature PAD.

title: Stent-graft placement for an axillosubclavian artery injury in a pediatric patient: A case report.
abstract: Axillosubclavian artery injury is a rare traumatic vascular injury associated with a high mortality rate. Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented. In this report, we present the case of a pediatric patient with traumatic axillosubclavian artery injury successfully treated with stent-graft placement. A 13-year-old boy was transported to a referring hospital following a traffic accident and transferred to our emergency and critical care center. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography conducted on hospital day 2 revealed a pseudoaneurysm due to right axillosubclavian artery injury, prompting endovascular stent-graft placement. The patient was discharged on hospital day 23. Although contrast-enhanced computed tomography at 1-year after discharge confirmed severe stenosis within the stent graft, distal perfusion was maintained. Notably, no ischemic symptoms or growth disturbances were observed in the right upper limb at the 3-year follow-up. Endovascular stent-graft placement appears to be a viable treatment for axillosubclavian artery injury in selected pediatric patients, particularly adolescents.

title: Ultralow-contrast stepping digital subtraction angiography for whole-limb arterial evaluation: A case report.
abstract: Stepping digital subtraction angiography (DSA) enables whole-limb arterial assessment with a single contrast injection, and diluted contrast medium may further reduce iodine exposure. A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach. Severe right external iliac artery stenosis prompted stepping DSA before and after embolization to evaluate distal embolization. Sevenfold- and tenfold-diluted stepping DSA examinations were performed before and after embolization, respectively, using identical injection parameters (3 mL/s; 30 mL). These required 4.29 and 3.0 mL of undiluted contrast medium, respectively. Although pedal artery enhancement was reduced with tenfold dilution, image quality remained acceptable, and no obvious distal embolization was identified in the visualized arteries; however, small emboli in poorly opacified pedal branches could not be excluded with tenfold dilution. Because internal iliac artery embolization was not expected to significantly alter lower-extremity arterial perfusion, the observed difference in image quality was considered to primarily reflect the difference between the two dilution protocols rather than changes in arterial hemodynamics. Ultralow-contrast stepping DSA may be a contrast-saving technique in selected cases when repeated whole-limb arterial evaluation is required.

Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach.

title: Delayed deterioration after surgical treatment of a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula detected by three spinal angiographies: Case report.
abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are the most common subtype of spinal arteriovenous malformations, and they often cause progressive myelopathy. Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. In this article, we report a case of T4 low-flow spinal DAVF that was only identified after three rounds of spinal angiography. The fistula was successfully occluded via surgery, and the patient's symptoms gradually improved postoperatively. Nevertheless, the patient later developed recurrent, aggravated symptoms. The delayed deterioration of previously resolved symptoms was attributed to venous thrombosis, and the condition improved after systemic anticoagulation therapy with heparin. The patients fluctuating symptoms stabilized one month after combined therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. For patients with a high clinical suspicion of spinal DAVF, required to confirm the final diagnosis. Delayed deterioration can occur secondary to progressive venous thrombosis, so preventive anticoagulation is indicated for selected patient's, and this intervention should be individualized.

Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition.

title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. Subsequently, a nomogram model was established, which was validated via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The DVT rate was 26.0%. Old age (OR, 1.0228), high American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (OR, 2.2764), greater blood loss (OR, 1.0015), blood transfusion (OR, 2.7917) and high D-dimer levels (OR, 1.0251) were identified as independent risk factors (P<0.05), while living in cities, high hemoglobin, high prealbumin, high Barthel index and high Braden scores served as protective factors (P<0.05). The model yielded an area under the curve value of 0.837. Additionally, the calibration curve showed high accuracy, and DCA validated the favorable clinical applicability of this predictive model. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.

A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed.

title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report.
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. Spectral Doppler sampling within the dissected segment showed a peak systolic velocity of 225 cm/s with spectral broadening. Initial CTA confirmed proximal celiac artery dissection. On short-interval repeat imaging, the maximum outer diameter at the same anatomic level increased from 8.8 mm to 9.7 mm, the true lumen became more compressed, and new false-lumen thrombosis appeared. Symptoms had not progressed; the decision to intervene was driven by imaging progression. False-lumen coil embolization and stent placement were performed. Follow-up CTA demonstrated a patent stent, preserved major branch perfusion, and no residual false-lumen opacification. In this patient, duplex ultrasound provided an initial imaging clue, whereas CTA confirmed the diagnosis, documented interval remodeling, and assessed the post-treatment anatomy.

title: [Primary and secondary microsurgical reconstruction in soft tissue sarcomas].
abstract: The reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection is sometimes essential to enable radical R0 resection, limb salvage, satisfactory functional outcomes and timely adjuvant treatment. In a retrospective cohort of 76 soft tissue reconstructions of the lower limbs, predominantly following external resections, wound coverage was consistently performed in a staged manner with a mean interval of 18 days; in more than half of the cases this interval was ≤14 days. A comprehensive review of the scientific literature on soft tissue reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection was conducted. Key prerequisites for maximum oncological safety and reconstructive reliability without delaying adjuvant therapy are plastic and reconstructive expertise within the sarcoma center, expedited pathological margin assessment and close collaboration with vascular surgery and radiotherapy.

title: Antiphospholipid syndrome: epidemiology and outcomes in the evolving criteria era.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a heterogeneous autoimmune thrombo-inflammatory disorder characterized by thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity and an expanding spectrum of microvascular, cardiac, haematological and other systemic manifestations. Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data. Antiphospholipid antibody positivity alone does not establish APS; transient or low-level positivity can occur without disease, whereas persistent antibodies must be interpreted alongside compatible clinical manifestations. Despite its rarity, APS causes substantial morbidity through recurrent thrombosis, organ damage and adverse pregnancy outcomes, supporting targeted evaluation in unprovoked or recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke in younger adults and selected pregnancy complications. Apparent differences among populations can reflect ascertainment, access to testing, study design and biological variation. Standardized case definitions, antibody testing and laboratory reporting, together with longitudinal population-based research in ancestry-diverse, paediatric and low-income and middle-income populations, are needed to refine estimates of APS burden and define its clinical spectrum.

title: Baricitinib Efficacy Through 4 Years in Responders and Safety up to 5 Years in Adults with Severe Alopecia Areata: Final Results from BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long-term efficacy and safety data are imperative for therapies used to treat severe alopecia areata (AA) because the disease is chronic, loss of response can be devastating to patients, and the safety profile needs to support long-term therapy. Baricitinib, a selective JAK inhibitor, has been approved for severe AA in adults and is being studied in pediatric patients. This study evaluates the final long-term efficacy and safety of baricitinib in adults with severe AA. METHODS: Efficacy was assessed for patients randomized to baricitinib 4 mg or 2 mg who achieved response (Severity of Alopecia Tool [SALT] score ≤ 20) at Week 52 (4 mg, N = 133; 2 mg, N = 72) and stayed on the same dose through Week 200. Proportions of patients maintaining a SALT score ≤ 20 and achieving a Clinician-Reported Outcome Measure for Eyebrow/Eyelash (EB/EL) Hair Loss™ score of 0 or 1 with ≥ 2-point improvement from baseline were reported using the modified last-observation-carried-forward method. Safety is reported as incidence rates (IR) per 100 patient-years at risk for the All BARI AA group (N = 1303) and Extended BARI AA group (N = 948) through 248 weeks of exposure RESULTS: For baricitinib 4 mg and 2 mg, respectively, among Week 52 responders, 115/133 (86.5%) and 61/72 (84.7%) maintained a SALT score ≤ 20 at Week 200. Regrowth of EB/EL hair continued beyond Week 52 and was maintained through Week 200. In up to 5 years of exposure with baricitinib, the IR for serious infections, nonmelanoma skin cancer malignancies, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and major adverse cardiovascular events remained low relative to background rates. No deaths occurred, and adverse event rates remained stable over time. CONCLUSIONS: Within this population, ~ 85% of responders maintained SALT scores ≤ 20 through approximately 4 years with continued benefit for EB/EL. Baricitinib's safety profile remained consistent over 5 years of treatment, in line with prior BRAVE program findings. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: BRAVE-AA1, ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03570749, start date, September 24, 2018; BRAVE-AA2, ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03899259, start date, July 8, 2019.

Baricitinib, a selective JAK inhibitor, has been approved for severe AA in adults and is being studied in pediatric patients. This study evaluates the final long-term efficacy and safety of baricitinib in adults with severe AA.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis is associated with adverse events in patients with high-grade carotid artery stenosis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), defined as the expansion of a subset of hematopoietic stem or progenitor cells driven by acquired mutations, represents a novel cardiovascular risk factor. Its role in patients with high-grade carotid stenosis remains to be evaluated. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) involving 30 genes implicated in CH was used as diagnostic-grade assay (SOPHiA DDM Myeloid Solution) to screen for CH in 83 prospectively collected patients with symptomatic or asymptomatic high-grade carotid stenosis undergoing carotid endarterectomy (CEA). RESULTS: P interaction Clonal markers were detected in 16 (19.7 %) of 83 patients (median age 71.2 years), with prevalence increasing at advanced age. At 5-year follow-up, CH carriers showed a higher cumulative incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; P = 0.040) compared to patients without CH; all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.57). Cox regression revealed a significant association between CH and MACE in a univariable model (P = 0.047), which remained significant after multivariable adjustment for age and sex (P = 0.018). Exploratory analyses suggested that the association between CH and MACE may differ according to carotid stenosis severity, with an increased incidence of MACE observed in patients with <90 % stenosis and concomitant CH, an effect absent in patients with ≥90 % stenosis ( = 0.03). DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: CH was associated with an adverse 5-year outcome in patients with carotid artery stenosis. These findings identify CH as a hematologic contributor to post-interventional cardiovascular risk and indicate that assessment of CH may offer additional prognostic information for residual risk stratification.

title: Cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen mapping on admission MRI may predict penumbral tissue fate in acute stroke patients treated successfully with thrombectomy.
abstract: PURPOSE: 2 Infarct growth occurs in most patients despite successful thrombectomy. We evaluated whether a dynamic susceptibility-contrast (DSC) perfusion-MRI surrogate of the cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO) improves prediction of tissue fate within perfusion-diffusion mismatch regions after successful thrombectomy. METHODS: 2 2 In this retrospective analysis of the prospective HIBISCUS-STROKE registry, we included anterior-circulation stroke patients with admission DSC perfusion MRI, recanalization (mTICI ≥ 2b) after thrombectomy, and day-6T2-FLAIR MRI. Admission DSC-derived CMRO, cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebral blood volume (CBV), and oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) were expressed as ratios to the mirrored contralateral region (rCMRO, rCBF, rCBV, rOEF) within mismatch subregions that infarcted (overlap with the day-6 lesion) or remained viable. All analyses accounted for within-patient clustering (generalized estimating equations, patient-level bootstrap and cross-validation). RESULTS: 2 2 2 Of 321 screened patients, 134 were included (median age, 71 years; 57.5 % men; median NIHSS score, 15), yielding 245 mismatch subregions (111 infarcted, 134 viable). rCMRO, rCBF, and rCBV were lower in infarcted than in viable subregions, whereas rOEF did not differ. rCMROprovided the best discrimination of infarction (AUC, 0.77; 95 % CI, 0.72-0.82), higher than rCBF (0.74; P = 0.04), rCBV (0.73; P = 0.001), and rOEF (0.52; P < 0.001); the gain over rCBF was modest (integrated discrimination improvement, 0.064; 95 % CI, 0.026-0.110). rCMRO<0.66 was selected in all cross-validation folds and independently predicted infarction (adjusted odds ratio, 8.02; 95 % CI, 4.60-14.01). CONCLUSIONS: 2 A DSC-MRI surrogate of CMROon admission discriminated infarct-destined from viable tissue within the perfusion-diffusion mismatch after successful thrombectomy, with a modest but consistent advantage over conventional perfusion metrics.

We evaluated whether a dynamic susceptibility-contrast (DSC) perfusion-MRI surrogate of the cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO) improves prediction of tissue fate within perfusion-diffusion mismatch regions after successful thrombectomy. METHODS: 2 2 In this retrospective analysis of the prospective HIBISCUS-STROKE registry, we included anterior-circulation stroke patients with admission DSC perfusion MRI, recanalization (mTICI ≥ 2b) after thrombectomy, and day-6T2-FLAIR MRI.

title: Comparison of recommendations for initial adult traumatic brain injury management across clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements: a scoping review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. We conducted a scoping review to identify, map, and compare recommendations for the initial medical management of adult TBI. METHODS: Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, guideline repositories, and gray literature for English or Spanish language documents published from 2010 to 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, charted recommendations across domains, and rated agreement using a priori categories; discrepancies were resolved by consensus or third reviewer. RESULTS: Sixteen documents met inclusion criteria, including guidelines, consensus statements, and best-practice recommendations. Broad agreement existed for early neurological assessment, airway protection, avoidance of hypotension and hypoxemia, and timely neuroimaging. Heterogeneity remained in blood pressure and cerebral perfusion pressure targets, repeat imaging, definitions of neurological deterioration, escalation criteria, observation protocols, and discharge processes. Anticonvulsant prophylaxis and venous thromboembolism prevention were inconsistently addressed. Blood-based biomarkers appeared in only three documents and were limited to computed tomography decision-making. CONCLUSIONS: Although the fundamental principles of care were largely consistent, important differences remain in their operational implementation. Greater harmonization of clinical definitions and management pathways may facilitate more consistent application of evidence-based recommendations across healthcare settings.

We conducted a scoping review to identify, map, and compare recommendations for the initial medical management of adult TBI. title: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae RkMsn4, a zinc finger transcription factor, regulates carotenoid and lipid metabolism to enhance tolerance to environmental stress in.
abstract: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Red yeasts serve as indispensable microbial resources for the production of carotenoids and lipids; however, environmental stress factors often limit their performance during industrial fermentation. The zinc-finger transcription factors Msn2/Msn4 act as central regulators of stress responses in yeasts. However, researchers have not yet systematically elucidated the similarities and differences in the mechanisms underlying the regulatory effects of Msn2/Msn4 under different stress conditions. In this study, we compared the shared and stress-specific regulatory functions of RkMsn4 inYM25235 under conditions of glucose starvation, 15 °C low temperature, and 4% NaCl salt stress. RkMsn4 contributed to the activity of the oxidative defense systems, including antioxidant enzymes, carotenoids, and glutathione, and the remodeling of membrane lipids, including phospholipids and unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs) across all three stress conditions. Additionally, RkMsn4 regulated stress-specific metabolic regulation by modulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) and aromatic amino acid (AAA) metabolism under glucose starvation conditions and promoting the utilization of exogenous sucrose and fructose under salt stress. By conducting weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified candidate genes potentially associated with carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide practical insights for improving tolerance to stress and metabolic productivity of red yeasts in industrial bioprocesses.IMPORTANCERed yeasts are important microorganisms for the production of carotenoids and lipids, but their performance is often limited by environmental stress. Understanding how red yeasts respond to environmental stress is crucial for advancing their application in industrial fermentation. This study reveals the stress response mechanisms mediated by the transcription factor RkMsn4 inYM25235 under glucose starvation, low temperature, and salt stress, as well as its regulatory role in carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the stress resistance and productivity of red yeasts in industrial applications.

title: Perioperative outcomes after thoracic aortic surgery in Johannesburg: a retrospective observational cohort study, 1995-2023.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thoracic aortic diseases require complex surgery, and outcomes data from African populations are scarce. We described the patient characteristic profile, documented risk factors, and perioperative outcomes of patients undergoing thoracic aortic surgery at a quaternary hospital in South Africa. METHODS: In a retrospective cohort study reported per the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines, we included patients aged 18 yr or older who underwent open thoracic aortic surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital between 1995 and 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. We assessed correlates using modified Poisson regression with robust variance (risk ratios [RRs]). RESULTS: P vs Of 366 patients (median age 48 yr [inter-quartile range 37-59]; 219 [59.8%] male), diagnoses were dissection in 157 (42.9%), aneurysm in 157 (42.9%), traumatic rupture in 26 (7.1%), and other in 26 (7.1%). In-hospital mortality was 21.9% (80 of 366; 95% confidence interval [CI] 17.7-26.4) and did not differ significantly across diagnosis groups (=0.693), being identical after dissection and aneurysm (22.9% in each). Prolonged operative duration (>600 min) was the only variable independently associated with mortality (adjusted RR 7.2; 95% CI 1.5-34.9), an imprecise, sparse-data estimate. Mortality was numerically higher in female than male patients (26.2%19.2%) but this difference was not significant after adjustment (adjusted RR 1.30; 95% CI 0.89-1.89); age and diagnosis were not independently associated. CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality after thoracic aortic surgery was 21.9%. Prolonged operative duration was associated with in-hospital mortality, although the estimate was imprecise, and operative duration is likely to be a marker of procedural complexity and adverse intraoperative course rather than an independently modifiable risk factor. The findings support intensive postoperative care.

title: Staged open ascending aortic replacement and endovascular total arch repair using a three-inner-branch physician-modified endograft for chronic postdissection aneurysms.
abstract: This report describes a single-admission, two-stage hybrid approach for chronic postdissection aneurysmal degeneration of the ascending aorta and aortic arch. Stage 1 consists of open ascending aortic replacement without deep hypothermic circulatory arrest. Stage 2 uses a three-inner-branch physician-modified endograft with novel features for total arch repair, relying on the surgical graft from stage 1 as the proximal landing zone. To minimize cardiac pulsatility-induced motion, atriocaval occlusion was used, alongside a repurposed thoracic branch endoprosthesis side branch for secure innominate artery sealing. This less invasive strategy simplifies arch reconstruction and broadens treatment options for high-risk patients with postdissection multisegment aneurysms.

title: Multiple recurrence of type III endoleak due to junctional component uncoupling of the AFX2 endograft accompanied with continuous aneurysmal sac regression.
abstract: Junctional component uncoupling of an AFX endograft is a rare but catastrophic cause of late type IIIA endoleak after endovascular aortic repair. A 74-year-old man presented with abdominal pain and shock 2 years and 8 months after endovascular aortic repair with AFX2, despite progressive sac regression on surveillance imaging. Computed tomography revealed aneurysm rupture due to a massive type IIIA endoleak with proximal component uncoupling. Emergency relining was performed; however, recurrent type III endoleaks required conversion to an aortouni-iliac configuration with femoral-femoral bypass. Retrospective imaging demonstrated progressive proximal intercomponent angle and reduced component overlap, suggesting longitudinal aortic remodeling as a mechanism of uncoupling.

title: Physician-modified fenestrated thoracic endovascular aortic repair for a rapidly developing infectious distal aortic arch aneurysm after intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin therapy.
abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis An 84-year-old man developed hemoptysis 3 weeks after receiving intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin therapy for bladder cancer. Computed tomography revealed a new saccular distal aortic arch aneurysm involving the origin of the left subclavian artery, with periaortic inflammation. Computed tomography performed 3 months earlier had shown no aneurysm. Urine polymerase chain reaction testing was positive for thecomplex, supporting the diagnosis of a bacillus Calmette-Guérin-related infectious aortic aneurysm. Given the prohibitive surgical risk, emergency endovascular repair was performed using a physician-modified fenestrated endograft with branch revascularization in combination with antituberculous therapy. Hemoptysis resolved, and no recurrence was observed at 1-year follow-up.

title: Zone 0 thoracic branch endoprosthesis with aortic arch debranching.
abstract: We present a case of staged arch debranching with subsequent zone 0 branched thoracic aortic endograft in a patient with a bovine arch. Open surgery is the historic gold standard for aortic arch repair. However, poor operative candidates may be unable to tolerate sternotomy and circulatory arrest required for repair. This case highlights a staged hybrid endovascular and open approach to repairing a progressively aneurysmal aortic arch.

title: Rare common femoral vein adventitial cystic disease presenting with lower-extremity swelling.
abstract: Adventitial cystic disease (ACD) is a rare, nonatherosclerotic disorder caused by mucin-filled cysts within the vessel wall that produce luminal compression. Venous ACD is uncommon and may mimic deep vein thrombosis. A 24-year-old woman presented with right leg pain and swelling from a 2.8-cm common femoral vein cyst. The patient underwent cyst excision and bovine patch venoplasty but developed postoperative thrombosis from venoplasty-site stenosis and hematoma compression. Thrombectomy and angioplasty failed, requiring venous stenting. Pathology confirmed ACD. The patient recovered on enoxaparin and clopidogrel. This case emphasizes confirming durable venous outflow after cyst excision.

title: Unexpected para-aortic venous migration of n-butyl cyanoacrylate during transarterial sac embolization for a type II endoleak: A technical pitfall.
abstract: We report an unusual case of para-aortic venous migration of n-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) during transarterial sac embolization for a type II endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair. Preprocedural computed tomography and angiography demonstrated no venous communication. During progressive NBCA injection, sequential opacification of the fourth lumbar vein and a para-aortic venous structure became apparent, prompting immediate cessation of embolization. The patient remained asymptomatic, and follow-up imaging demonstrated stable aneurysm size without complications. This case highlights a rare technical pitfall and emphasizes careful fluoroscopic monitoring during NBCA sac embolization despite initially negative imaging findings.

title: High BMI-attributable burden of eight diseases relevant to the CKM framework in China: GBD 2023 estimates and projections to 2050.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a recently defined clinical entity integrating metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Elevated body mass index (BMI) is a major modifiable risk factor for CKM syndrome, yet comprehensive long-term analyses of the high BMI-attributable burden in China remain scarce. METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study, we assessed the burden of eight selected CKM-related diseases attributable to high BMI (atrial fibrillation and flutter [AFF], chronic kidney disease due to hypertension [CKD-HTN] or diabetes mellitus type 2 [CKD-T2DM], diabetes mellitus type 2 [T2DM], hypertensive heart disease [HHD], ischemic heart disease [IHD], lower extremity peripheral arterial disease [LEPAD], and stroke) in China from 1990 to 2023. The primary outcomes were absolute deaths and DALYs and their age-standardized rates (ASRs) per 100,000 population. Joinpoint regression and ARIMA models were applied to analyze and project temporal trends in ASRs, age-period-cohort analysis was conducted using age-specific rates, and decomposition analysis quantified the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological change to changes in absolute deaths and DALYs. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, absolute deaths and DALYs for all eight selected diseases relevant to the CKM framework increased. IHD had the highest burden in 2023 (114,980 deaths; 2,923,595 DALYs), whereas AFF showed the greatest relative increase (11.4-fold). Descriptively, men generally had higher point estimates of death and DALY counts, ASMRs, and ASDRs for CKD-T2DM, CKD-HTN, IHD, and HHD, whereas women had higher corresponding estimates for AFF. Joinpoint regression identified sustained increases in AFF, IHD, T2DM, and LEPAD, with several inflection points around 2005. APC analysis showed pronounced age-related gradients and variations in period and cohort rate ratios. Decomposition analysis indicated that population aging was the predominant contributor to increasing mortality for most outcomes, while epidemiological change had heterogeneous effects and partially offset increases in CKD-T2DM and HHD. Model-based projections suggested heterogeneous future trajectories: increasing mortality and DALY rates for AFF, IHD, and LEPAD; increasing DALYs but slightly declining mortality for T2DM; broadly stable or slightly declining rates for stroke, CKD-T2DM, and CKD-HTN; and declining point estimates for HHD, although with substantial long-term uncertainty. CONCLUSION: High BMI-attributable stage 2-4 CKM burden has risen sharply in China and will continue to increase, driven mainly by worsening epidemiological risks. AFF, IHD, and LEPAD show the fastest growth. Men had higher age-standardized mortality and DALY rates for several selected diseases. Early-life obesity prevention and sex-tailored interventions are urgently needed.

title: [Resection of locally advanced soft tissue sarcomas of the extremities : Surgical strategies to avoid postoperative complications].
abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas of the extremities are rare malignant tumors that constitute less than 1% of all malignant diseases. The aim of multimodal treatment is the complete surgical removal of the tumor into healthy tissue in the sense of an R0 resection. Due to the possible proximity to skin, blood vessels, nerves and bone, locally advanced sarcomas necessitate a specialized interdisciplinary treatment planning which leads to a complete resection of the sarcoma and also ensures a maximum preservation of function or limb. To achieve this, vascular surgical and plastic reconstructive interventions must be taken into consideration. Furthermore, postoperative complications, such as wound healing disorders, seromas and infections must be avoided in order not to delay the rehabilitation. This article summarizes the practice-oriented principles of the surgical treatment for locally advanced sarcomas of the extremities with a focus on the reduction of postoperative morbidity.

title: Methylene blue-guided parenchyma-sparing ex vivo resection and autotransplantation for a type III renal arteriovenous fistula with large renal vein aneurysm: A technical case report.
abstract: High-flow renal arteriovenous malformations (AVMs), type III with vein aneurysms, are rare and often require nephrectomy. A 54-year-old man presented with lumbar pain and hematuria. Computed tomography angiography revealed an 8- × 12-cm right renal vein aneurysm and a type III arteriovenous fistula occupying >30% of the kidney. After ex vivo nephrectomy with cold perfusion, selective methylene blue injection delineated the AVM nidus and parenchyma, guiding resection and excision. The procedure was performed by a multidisciplinary team including a vascular surgeon, transplant surgeon, and urologist. The kidney was reconstructed and reimplanted. Postoperative creatinine levels stabilized at 1.10 mg/dL, and computed tomography angiography confirmed AVM exclusion and preserved perfusion. Methylene blue mapping can enable parenchyma-sparing repair in selected cases.

title: Intravascular ultrasound-guided repair of delayed traumatic popliteal artery occlusion using an interwoven nitinol stent.
abstract: Traumatic popliteal artery occlusion is a limb-threatening condition traditionally managed with open surgical revascularization. Here, we describe a 66-year-old man with delayed occlusion after high-energy lower-extremity trauma. Initial computed tomography angiography indicated preserved flow despite severe arterial deformation. Progressive heel necrosis developed after fracture fixation and debridement; repeat imaging on day 24 showed complete occlusion of the popliteal artery. Intravascular ultrasound-guided endovascular repair with an interwoven nitinol stent restored antegrade flow. Wound healing was achieved after flap and skin graft procedures, and stent patency was maintained for >2.5 years.

title: [Isolated limb perfusion to avoid mutilating surgical resections].
abstract: Isolated limb perfusion (ILP) represents a regional oncological therapeutic approach, predominantly applied in the management of locally advanced soft tissue sarcomas of the extremities and malignant melanomas. The technique involves temporary vascular isolation of the affected limb from the systemic circulation, followed by perfusion under strictly controlled hyperthermic conditions using a cytotoxic agent combination, most commonly melphalan in conjunction with human recombinant tumor necrosis factor-alpha. The primary objective of ILP is to achieve high locoregional drug concentrations while limiting systemic exposure, thereby promoting substantial tumor regression and enabling limb preservation. The most commonly reported procedure-related complications include regional and systemic perfusion reactions and postoperative compartment syndrome. When performed in high-volume specialized centers, ILP is regarded as a safe and efficacious treatment modality, with limb preservation rates of up to 93% reported in soft tissue sarcomas.

title: Comorbidities and infectious episodes in multiple sclerosis patients within general practices in the Netherlands.
abstract: BACKGROUND: People with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) are at heightened risk of comorbidities and infections, due to the disease's debilitating nature and side effects of disease-modifying therapies (DMT). METHODS: This retrospective case-control study was conducted the Dutch Nivel Primary Care Database from the year 2019, assessing chronic comorbidities and infections in PwMS versus matched controls. The influence of the comorbidity burden (evaluated by the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)) and infections on mortality was evaluated using Cox regression. RESULTS: A higher lifetime prevalence of chronic diseases in PwMS was found, in particular for osteoporosis, stroke, epilepsy, peripheral artery disease, glaucoma, depression and certain oncological diseases (e.g. kidney, hematological, skin cancers). Comorbidity burden was higher in male PwMS, older age, prolonged disease duration, and lower socio-economic status (SES). The crude annual infection rate was higher in PwMS than in matched controls (OR 1.86; 95% CI 1.73 - 1.99). CCI scores of 1 and ≥2 were associated with significantly increased 5-year mortality (aHR 1.86 and 3.30, respectively), as was having at least one infectious episode in 2019 (aHR 1.68). DISCUSSION: PwMS have more chronic comorbidities and are at a considerable heightened risk of infections. Prevention, early detection and treatment of comorbidities may ameliorate prognosis of MS and the presence of comorbidities should be part of individualized DMT MS patient care.

METHODS: This retrospective case-control study was conducted the Dutch Nivel Primary Care Database from the year 2019, assessing chronic comorbidities and infections in PwMS versus matched controls. The influence of the comorbidity burden (evaluated by the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)) and infections on mortality was evaluated using Cox regression.

title: Incidence of Deep Vein Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism in Patients with Hidradenitis Suppurativa.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The risk of thromboembolism in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) has not been established. This study aimed to estimate the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) among adults with HS and demographic subgroups. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2024, using a health insurance claims database (Optum Clinformatics DataMart) in the US. Adults aged ≥ 18 years with an outpatient visit linked to a diagnosis of HS or any other diagnosis (controls) were eligible. Patients with prior diagnosis of either outcome or associated conditions were excluded. The primary outcomes evaluated were new-onset DVT and PE. RESULTS: Mean (SD) age was 43 (16) years for eligible patients with HS (n = 44,520) and 54 (19) years for control patients (n = 3,792,627). Incidence of DVT was 3.0 (95% CI 2.5-3.4) and 3.5 (95% CI 3.4-3.5) per 1000 person-years (PY) in patients with HS and controls, respectively. Incidence of PE was 2.4 (95% CI 2.0-2.8) and 2.2 (95% CI 2.2-2.3) per 1000 PY in patients with HS and controls, respectively. In demographics-adjusted analyses, standardized incidence ratios for DVT and PE were 1.42 (95% CI 1.23-1.65) and 1.78 (95% CI 1.50-2.10), respectively. Comorbidity-adjusted hazard ratios for DVT and PE were 1.12 (95% CI 0.97-1.31) and 1.35 (95% CI 1.14-1.60), respectively. Incidence of DVT was higher in patients with HS by a factor of 1.5-2.9 for age subgroups between 45 and 74 years, with absolute incidence rates ranging from 3.5 to 8.8 per 1000 PY. Incidence of PE was higher in patients with HS by a factor of 1.5-3.2 across age subgroups between 45 and 74 years, with absolute incidence rates ranging from 3.0 to 5.4 per 1000 PY. CONCLUSION: Patients with HS have a significantly higher incidence of both DVT and PE relative to demographically similar patients without HS. This information may support counseling on risk mitigation strategies and safety monitoring during treatment and may provide context for observed (versus expected) thrombotic events in clinical trials for HS.
